originalAdoptionRow.note: American Samoa adopts the federal income-tax rules as the separate Samoan Income Tax, a territorial income tax with withholding on wages.

originalGraduatedRow.note: The American Samoa Government Tax Office publishes the IRS 2000 Tax Table and Instructions for use with Form 390, with graduated rates (15 percent and up); IRS Publication 570 (2025) says its tax laws are modeled on the Internal Revenue Code with certain differences.

originalAdoptionRow.note: The Guam Organic Act applies the federal income-tax laws in Guam as a separate Guam Territorial income tax payable to the government of Guam, so wages are taxed.

originalGraduatedRow.note: IRS Publication 570 (2025) says Guam has its own tax system based on the same tax laws and tax rates that apply in the United States (seven graduated federal brackets); the Guam Department of Revenue and Taxation administers it as the Guam Territorial Income Tax.

unsupportedTerritorySchedules.gap: Not covered by the existing2026 single-filer schedule source; no territorial statute/rate or current-game peer estimate is supplied by this packet.

originalAdoptionRow.note: The Commonwealth adopts the Internal Revenue Code as the Northern Marianas Territorial Income Tax, a broad income tax on wages.

originalGraduatedRow.note: The CNMI wage and salary tax (4 CMC 1204, from PL 9-22) applies rates from 2 to 9 percent by wage level, and 4 CMC 1701 adopts the Internal Revenue Code as the Northern Marianas Territorial Income Tax.

unsupportedTerritorySchedules.gap: Not covered by the existing2026 single-filer schedule source; no territorial statute/rate or current-game peer estimate is supplied by this packet.

originalAdoptionRow.cite: Ley 1-2011 (Internal Revenue Code for a New Puerto Rico)
originalAdoptionRow.note: Puerto Rico taxes individual income under its own Internal Revenue Code of 2011, with a graduated schedule reaching 33 percent.

originalGraduatedRow.note: Hacienda 2025 individual return instructions give graduated normal-tax brackets of 0, 7, 14, 25 and 33 percent under section 1021.01; no 2026 change to a single rate was found.

originalAdoptionRow.note: The federal income tax laws are in force in the Virgin Islands as its own income tax on wages, with the proceeds paid to the territory.

originalGraduatedRow.note: IRS Publication 570 (2025) says the USVI has its own tax system based on the same tax laws and tax rates that apply in the United States, so wages face the graduated federal schedule; residents file Form 1040 with the Virgin Islands Bureau of Internal Revenue.
